iOS приложение все ни как не может пройти ревью
Hello,

Thank you for your resubmission, but we need additional information before we can continue our review.

Please reply to this message in App Store Connect with detailed answers to the questions below.

Review Environment
Submission ID: 2b27f1e4-9f5e-4f50-803e-f14fe3ca48dc
Review date: September 08, 2026
Review Device: iPad Air 11-inch (M3)
Version reviewed: 0.5.0 (37)

Guideline 2.1 - Information Needed

We need a demo video that demonstrates the current version, 0.5.0, in use on a physical iOS device.

The provided demo video must show the following features and functionality in the app: 

- All the CallKit services supported in the app.

The demo video must also: 

- Show the app running on a physical iOS device, not on a simulator. A screen recorder can be used to capture footage of the app in use.
- Clearly document all relevant app features, services, and user permission requests.

Next Steps

- Provide a link to the demo video in the Notes Field on the App Review Information section of your the app’s page in App Store Connect and reply to this message. Note that if the app can only be reviewed with a demo video, updated demo videos will need to be provided for every app submission.
- If there are no changes and the video remains the same as previous versions of the app, use the Notes field of the App Review Information section in App Store Connect to confirm that the video remains valid for all storefronts.

Resources

To learn more about providing information in App Store Connect, see App Store Connect Help.
Support
- Reply to this message in your preferred language if you need assistance. If you need additional support, use the Contact Us module.
- Consult with fellow developers and Apple engineers on the Apple Developer Forums.
- Provide feedback on this message and your review experience by completing a short survey.

Test on the latest betas
Betas of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, tvOS 27 and visionOS 27 are now available. Download the latest betas to prepare your app for upcoming software releases. Learn more about installing and using Apple beta software.

== rejected ==
---
name: ios-rejected-needs-hardware-demo-video
description: "iOS 0.5.0 was rejected twice on one submission — first Guideline 2.1 (hardware demo video), then 2.1(a) (demo account); the video is explicitly not enough"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: aca6f761-c092-41de-8311-28bc262a7290
  modified: 2026-09-04T18:34:22.782Z
---

App Review rejected iOS 0.5.0 (build 37) **twice on the same submission**
`2b27f1e4-9f5e-4f50-803e-f14fe3ca48dc`. macOS 0.5.0 was approved from the same code on 2026-08-29
(submission `41b10c68`), so both demands belong to the iOS reviewer, not to the account.

**Round 1, 2026-09-01 — Guideline 2.1.** They asked for a demo video of the current build on a physical
device, with the initial pairing and the whole workflow. `docs/media/demo.mp4` answered it, linked from the
review notes.

**Round 2, 2026-09-03 — Guideline 2.1(a).** The reviewer ran the build on an iPad Pro 11-inch (M4), selected
the "HF" segment on the Connect screen, met the huggingface.co login page and stopped. The letter says
outright that **a demo video is not sufficient** — so round 1's answer does not carry over. The formal
trigger was `demoAccountRequired: false` in App Review Information beside a live sign-in screen: any way in
that asks for credentials needs credentials in that section, whatever else the notes offer.

**Why the simulator did not cover it:** the notes already pointed at `ConnectRoute.simulator` and the reviewer
read them. A demonstration mode answers "show us the features"; it does not answer "let us in". Both halves
of 2.1(a) need their own answer — credentials for the account, the simulator for pre-populated content.

**How it was closed (2026-09-04, no new build):** a throwaway Hugging Face account
(`alexey1312ru+hfreview@gmail.com`, no 2FA, plus-alias because HF refuses a second account on one address),
`demoAccountRequired: true`, and notes rewritten to open with the account rather than with the simulator.
The account has **no robot linked**, so "Your Reachies" shows `No Reachy online` — the notes name that screen
as the correct result, which turns an empty list from "we could not verify" into the proof that nothing else
hides behind the sign-in.

**Sharing the real robot was refused and stays refused.** A robot linked to a demo account gives a stranger
its camera and microphone in a private home, for an unpredictable multi-day review window. Do not offer it.

**Held in reserve for a third round:** the approved macOS build of the same source, as the control that the
app is reviewable and the account is healthy.

**Update Review re-stamps the submission.** `submittedDate` on `2b27f1e4` moved to 2026-09-04T17:52Z and the
state went to `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW` — same submission id, same build. Save the review notes **before** replying
in the Resolution Center and before pressing the button, or the reviewer comes back to the old ones.
The rejection text itself is only in the Resolution Center: the API reports `REJECTED` / `UNRESOLVED_ISSUES`
with no message. See [[review-notes-live-only-in-asc]] and [[app-store-submission-gates]].
== review-notes ==
---
name: review-notes-live-only-in-asc
description: App Review and Beta App Review notes live only on the server, so they silently fall behind the build; editing them does not reset the review queue
metadata:
  type: project
---

App Review notes, Beta App Review notes and the TestFlight page description are
stored only in App Store Connect — nothing in this repository holds them, so no
diff and no CI job can catch them going stale. On 2026-08-31 all three still said
"HARDWARE REQUIRED … There is no demo mode, no mock data and no test account" and
named the Connect screen's third segment "Manual", while 0.5.0 had shipped
`ConnectRoute.simulator` and the App Store description already advertised
"TRY IT WITHOUT A ROBOT". The reviewer was reading that the app could not be
evaluated at all.

**Why:** a reviewer who cannot exercise the app is the usual cause of a long
Waiting for Review and of a Guideline 2.1 rejection. macOS 0.5.0 cleared review in
hours on 2026-08-29; iOS, submitted four minutes later, was still queued two days
on.

**How to apply:** re-read the notes against the build whenever a release adds a way
in that needs no robot. `asc review details-for-version --version-id …` for App
Review, `asc testflight review view --app …` for the beta pair. Editing notes with
`review details-update` while the version sits in WAITING_FOR_REVIEW is safe — the
state and `submittedDate` on the reviewSubmission both stayed put, so the queue
position is not lost. Replacing the build would reset it. Also note that
`versions list` prints the version record's `createdDate`, which reads as a much
older submission than the real one — the date that matters is
`submittedDate` on `review submissions-list`. See [[app-store-submission-gates]]
and [[asc-review-submit-manual-finish]].
== testflight-highest ==
---
name: testflight-picks-highest-build-number
description: TestFlight shows the build with the highest CFBundleVersion, not the newest upload, so a lower build number hides a newer version
metadata:
  type: project
---

TestFlight offers testers the build with the **highest CFBundleVersion**, not the
most recent upload and not the highest marketing version. On 2026-09-01 iOS 0.5.0
was build 40 while 0.4.2 was build 177, so the public TestFlight page kept showing
0.4.2 — although build 40 was VALID, BETA_APPROVED and in the Public Beta group.
macOS was correct at the same moment (0.5.0 = build 180 > 177).

App Store Connect does not catch this: it only demands a rising CFBundleVersion
**inside one marketing version on one platform**, so 40 was accepted after 39.

The iOS 0.5.0 builds are 37, 38, 39, 40 — Xcode Cloud's own counter, not the
`COMMIT_COUNT + CI_BUILD_NUMBER` that `Apps/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh` stamps
(that would give ~226, and the script fails loudly if its sed matches nothing or
the count is at or below BUILD_NUMBER_FLOOR=150). So the number the script writes
does not reach the artifact — suspect "Xcode Cloud manages build numbers" in App
Store Connect. Read `Archiving build N` in the Xcode Cloud log to confirm.

**Why:** a green upload and an approved beta review still leave testers on the old
version, and nothing in the API reports it as a problem.

**How to apply:** compare build numbers across marketing versions, not dates, when
TestFlight looks stale. Fix by uploading a local release ([[verify-testflight-upload]]),
whose number is `git rev-list --count HEAD` and therefore above every Xcode Cloud one.
== ios waits ==
---
name: ios-0-4-0-waits-on-0-3-0-review
description: iOS is deliberately not submitted to the App Store — it waits for the verdict on 0.3.0, in review since 2026-08-17; only TestFlight ships on iOS
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-08-19 macOS **0.4.1** went to review (version `c7f715a4-a340-4a1c-bf7c-820d67b509b5`,
build 164) while **iOS was left unsubmitted on purpose**. iOS 0.3.0 has been in
`WAITING_FOR_REVIEW` since 2026-08-17 and App Store Connect refuses a second version in
review, so submitting iOS would mean cancelling 0.3.0 and losing its place in the queue.
Both platforms carry build 164 on TestFlight.

**Why:** iOS has never been approved, so 0.3.0's verdict decides two things at once — the
first live iOS version, and whether `whatsNew` is accepted on iOS at all.

**How to apply:** check `asc versions list --app 6799644194` first. Once 0.3.0 resolves,
submit iOS the same way macOS went: `versions create --platform IOS`, `metadata push`
(drop `whatsNew` if iOS is still unapproved), `review details-update` with the simulator
notes, then the manual submission finish in [[asc-review-submit-manual-finish]].
While 0.3.0 sits in review the app carries two app infos, so `asc validate` cannot answer
at all — check age rating and screenshots by hand. See [[app-store-submission-gates]].
== rename version ==
---
name: rename-version-instead-of-creating-one
description: A withdrawn App Store version is renamed with `versions update --version`, which keeps review details, screenshots and localizations that a new version would lose
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

To re-release a version that was pulled out of review, **rename it** rather than create a
new one: `asc submit cancel --id <submission>` leaves the version in `DEVELOPER_REJECTED`,
which is editable, and `asc versions update --version-id <id> --version 0.4.1` moves it to
the new number. Measured on 2026-08-19 for macOS 0.4.0 → 0.4.1: the App Review Information
(contacts and the `com.apple.security.network.server` justification), all six screenshots
and the version localization survived untouched. Only the attached build detaches.

**Why:** App Review Information is per version and per platform, lives only on the server,
and is absent from `metadata/`. A fresh `versions create` starts empty and every one of
those records has to be written again.

**How to apply:** cancel → `versions update --version` → `metadata push` for the changed
fields → `versions attach-build` → submit. Verify the notes survived with
`asc review details-for-version --version-id <id>` before submitting.
See [[asc-review-submit-manual-finish]].
== manual finish ==
---
name: asc-review-submit-manual-finish
description: `asc review submit` needs --build and dies on a request timeout, leaving an empty draft; finish it with items-add --item-type appStoreVersions and submissions-submit
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`asc review submit` failed twice on 2026-08-19 (asc 3.7.0) before macOS 0.4.1 reached review:

1. Without `--build <build-id>` it exits on `Error: --build is required`, even when the
   build is already attached to the version.
2. With it, the `POST /v1/reviewSubmissionItems` call hit `context deadline exceeded` and
   preserved an **empty** draft submission.

Finish that draft by hand — the item type is not obvious:

```bash
export ASC_TIMEOUT=120s
asc review items-list --submission <sub>                                    # confirm it is empty
asc review items-add --submission <sub> --item-type appStoreVersions --item-id <version-id>
asc review submissions-submit --id <sub> --confirm
asc versions list --app 6799644194                                          # WAITING_FOR_REVIEW
```

**Why:** the wrapper's three inner calls are each retryable, but a half-run leaves a draft
that later reads as stale. Reusing it costs nothing and avoids that.

**How to apply:** read the outcome off the version state, never off the exit code — which is
the same rule the false-negative documented in `docs/release.md` needs.

#
#   mise run asc -- apps list

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
Отказ не про фичи — он про `UIBackgroundModes: voip` в `Apps/Project.swift:117`. `Sources/ReachyMedia/AGENTS.md:44-46` это уже предсказал дословно: «Declaring `voip` without PushKit is a question App Review can ask». Ревьюер увидел ключ, не нашёл звонков в старом видео и попросил доказать, что VoIP реальный.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Вспомнил. Это **третий** раунд по одной submission `2b27f1e4` (0.5.0 build 37): 2.1 → видео, 2.1(a) → демо-аккаунт, теперь 2.1 → CallKit. Текущее состояние проверил:

- версия iOS 0.5.0 — `REJECTED`, id `2d312612-4085-4323-a751-9b737b6d0a9f`;
- notes в ASC уже с демо-аккаунтом и ссылкой на `demo.mp4`;
- **старое видео звонков не показывает** — по его же описанию в notes: pairing, Robot tab, audio settings, Moves tab. 61 секунда, ни одного звонка.

Так что просьба законная: нового билда не нужно, нужно новое видео.

## Что показать в видео

Все системные звонковые сервисы приложения (LiveCommunicationKit, не старый CallKit — это важно назвать в ответе):

| # | Что | Где в коде |
|---|-----|-----------|
| 1 | Запрос разрешения микрофона | перед `StartConversationAction` |
| 2 | Старт звонка — тап «Unmute microphone» в Camera viewport | `CameraViewport.swift:144` |
| 3 | Системный UI звонка — pill в Dynamic Island, зелёный индикатор | `RobotCallController` |

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
`CallActivity.donate` — то, из-за чего Recents обязательно должны быть в кадре: приложение жертвует `INStartCallIntent`, значит для системы это полноценный звонковый клиент, и ревьюер вправе ждать, что строка в Phone работает. Это как раз тот «сервис», который нельзя показать симулятором.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Готовы два черновика:

- `.../scratchpad/review-notes.txt` — новый текст App Review Notes, 3691 символ (лимит 4000), с секцией **CALL SERVICES** и плейсхолдерами `M:SS` под таймкоды
- `.../scratchpad/resolution-reply.txt` — ответ в Resolution Center

Память обновил: в `ios-rejected-needs-hardware-demo-video.md` теперь записан раунд 3.

## От тебя — одно: видео

Снимай на **iPhone**, не на iPad: системная звонковая pill там заметна, на iPad её видно хуже. Запись экрана + робот в кадре, порядок как в таблице выше. Минуты полторы хватит.

Обязательно в кадре: разрешение микрофона, старт по «Unmute microphone», mute **из системного UI** (чтобы было видно, как кнопка в приложении следует за ним), завершение из системного UI, второй звонок и завершение через «End call», и Phone → Recents с redial.

Скинь файл — я положу его в `docs/media/demo.mp4` (сайт уже раздаёт его как `video/mp4`, GitHub raw бы не смог), впишу реальные таймкоды, сохраню notes через `asc review details-update`, проверю их чтением, и только потом отправлю ответ в Resolution Center. Новый билд не нужен — версия остаётся 0.5.0 (37), Update Review просто перештампует ту же submission.

Альтернатива — выкинуть `voip` и вместе с ним всю интеграцию #78 из iOS. Не советую: без ключа `ConversationManager.perform` кидает `unentitled`, двусторонний звук деградирует до голого микрофона, и это стоит нового билда плюс потери места в очереди.
